items.title: Foundations and the domain
items.snippet: A domain is the tenant. Campaigns come after skills, users, lists, dispositions, and a profile.

items.title: A contact center is not a phone system

items.title: The domain is the tenant

items.snippet: Quote the document. Quote the clock. Do not invent a percent or a coverage map.

items.title: 911 is a location, not a prefix
items.snippet: The E911 data sheet says agents dial 911 directly, with no prefix, and that the service sends a dispatchable location. It names the United States and its territories, Kari's Law, and RAY BAUM'S Act. The partner named on that sheet is RedSky

items.title: The address has to be the room they are in
items.snippet: A dispatchable location is the place responders can find a person. A headquarters address while the agent is at home is the failure the EULA describes. Remote and hybrid floors have to register the location the agent is actually using. MyE9

items.title: Recording is the customer's duty too
items.snippet: The EULA treats recordings as customer data. It says calls can be recorded while the caller is on hold and after a transfer. It puts notice and consent on the customer, who has to follow the laws that apply to their calls. This lab will not

items.title: Retention is several clocks
items.snippet: The public retention page splits the clocks. VCC audio is the sooner of 30 days, a successful SFTP or FTP offload, or the contract. E911 recordings are 30 days. Agent data is 60 days. Campaign state is 120 days. A disabled domain is 120 day

items.title: Attestation is not an ANI field
items.snippet: Certified Caller is Five9's published STIR/SHAKEN program, tied to FCC and CRTC expectations. A campaign profile that overrides ANI changes what you present. It does not, by itself, mean the call is attested. Say 'we set local ANI' or 'we a

items.title: Abandon rate is a regulated posture
items.snippet: Default campaign settings call out a warning if you change Max Abandoned Call Percentage. Other fields on that page include Max Queue Time, Show Out of Numbers Alert, Monitor Abandoned Call Percentage, Call Analysis, Voice Detection level,

items.title: TCPA manual touch is a physical control
items.snippet: On domains where TCPA manual touch is enabled, other dialing modes are not available. Agents type the external number. Paste and drag are blocked. Dial enables only when the typed number matches. If preview times out, the agent goes Not Rea

items.title: Ecosystem
items.snippet: Every box needs a link. Every word needs a page or a local label.

items.title: The domain has neighbors
items.snippet: A Five9 domain does not live alone. Voice arrives on a SIP story. Agents sit in a desktop. WEM or a partner workforce suite watches the roster. A CRM pops. GenAI Studio may draft a summary. E911 carries a location. Reports leave through a r

items.title: Workforce, quality, and the recording shelf
items.snippet: The WEM product page describes workforce management, quality, analytics, surveys, and recording, and it also describes a Verint partnership. Five9 says it manages install and upgrades for the solution it delivers. The data sheet is the shor

items.title: Analytics and the report that is not a dashboard rumor
items.snippet: Analytics shows up on the WEM page and inside reporting. They are not one button. Standard reports need the Reporting role. Categories include ACD Queue, Campaign, Call Log, and the rest of that list. Layouts are tabular, summary, and matri

items.title: AI agents are a handoff with a name
items.snippet: Five9 Engage talks about self-service and the agent desktop together. Studio holds a digital IVA task. GenAI Studio is where knowledge and prompts are tested, and the product page says it powers Five9 AI applications, starting with Agent As

items.title: The glossary is the contract with yourself
items.snippet: Teams lose hours to words that Five9 uses narrowly: domain, skill, campaign profile, DNIS, disposition, list penetration, vertical dialing, campaign, autodial, blended, manual touch. The ecosystem glossary in this lab defines the ones we co

items.title: Read the map before you add a box
items.snippet: Integration maps fail when a logo is enough. Salesforce in the IVR is a module. Salesforce on the desktop is an adapter. Certified Caller is not the ANI. RedSky is not the ITSP. Verint is not automatically your WEM. Studio regions are not E

items.title: Certifications and practice
items.snippet: No invented exam codes. The sales badge is a sales badge. Date every number.

items.title: University is a catalog, not a secret exam code
items.snippet: Five9 University is the public training front door: online classes, webinars, instructor-led classes, train-the-trainer, and custom programs. The curriculum brief this lab read is dated April 2023. Treat the mix of courses as a dated brochu

items.title: Practice is the domain, not the badge
items.snippet: The objects you must be able to touch are the ones in the planning topic and the IVR chapter: skill groups, users, lists, dispositions, profiles, campaigns, and modules. A certification that never had you start a stopped inbound campaign di

items.title: What this lab will not pretend to be
items.snippet: Five9 Lab is an independent study floor. It is not Five9, not a partner portal, and not a place that can change your domain. The builder's JSON is not an import. The pacing chart is not the dialer. The 3D topology is a picture of failure, n

items.title: Domain
items.snippet: The VCC tenant. Skills, users, lists, and campaigns stay inside it.

items.title: Skill group
items.snippet: Agents or supervisors who can take a campaign's work. A user and a campaign can have more than one.

items.title: User profile
items.snippet: The permission template for a person. Not a campaign profile.

items.title: Campaign profile
items.snippet: Overrides defaults such as ANI. One profile is assigned to a campaign. The same profile can be reused.

items.title: Campaign
items.snippet: Inbound, outbound, or autodial. Blended is staffing language, not a fourth type.

items.title: DNIS
items.snippet: The number an inbound campaign answers. A stopped campaign does not answer.

items.title: Disposition
items.snippet: The outcome code on a call. Final disposition stops the other numbers on that record for the campaign.

items.title: List penetration
items.snippet: The default list walk: first number on every record, then the next number.

items.title: Vertical dialing
items.snippet: Finishes the numbers on one record before moving on. Community notes say the compass wording is easy to misread.

items.title: Preview
items.snippet: The agent sees CRM history before the dial.

items.title: Progressive
items.snippet: The outbound page describes one customer call per available agent. The dialer page also says adaptive pace. Quote the page you mean.

items.title: Power
items.snippet: A configured number of calls per agent, with an abandon throttle.

items.title: Predictive
items.snippet: Algorithmic pacing. Product guidance talks about teams larger than about ten agents.

items.title: Manual touch
items.snippet: No automatic dial. TCPA manual touch adds typing, blocks paste, and enables Dial on a match.

items.title: Max Abandoned Call Percentage
items.snippet: A campaign field with a warning if you change it. This lab does not state a numeric default.

items.title: IVR module
items.snippet: A named block in the IVR Administrator's Guide, such as Menu, Play, If/Else, or Skill Transfer.

items.title: Skill Transfer
items.snippet: Sends the call toward one or more skills. No skill selected means the Default queue in the community write-up.

items.title: Default queue
items.snippet: Where a Skill Transfer with no skill goes, per the community article.

items.title: Call variable
items.snippet: Reportable only after the edit permission and the reporting flag. Not historical.

items.title: Reporting role
items.snippet: Required, with a reporting permission, before standard reports appear.

items.title: Call log
items.snippet: A report with filters. A July 2026 community article describes about 60 days unless retention is extended.

items.title: Web2Campaign
items.snippet: One of the API names on the APIs and SDKs page.

items.title: CRM SDK
items.snippet: The path for a CRM that is not a named Plus adapter.

items.title: Web Connector
items.snippet: Opens a URL. Not the same object as a Plus adapter.

items.title: Plus adapter
items.snippet: The listed CRM integrations, using HTTPS and Secure WebSocket.

items.title: G.711
items.snippet: The default codec in the technical requirements, described as uncompressed.

items.title: DNS SRV
items.snippet: The preferred lookup for SIP targets in the technical requirements.

items.title: TLS 1.2
items.snippet: The required TLS version. TLS 1.1 is not supported.

items.title: Direct Connect
items.snippet: Layer-3 handoff, full duplex, BGP failover, in the technical requirements.

items.title: Certified Caller
items.snippet: Five9's STIR/SHAKEN program. Not the same thing as a local ANI on a profile.

items.title: E911
items.snippet: Direct 911 with a dispatchable location. The data sheet names RedSky.

items.title: Dispatchable location
items.snippet: The place responders can find the caller. A stale HQ address fails that test.

items.title: MyE911
items.snippet: Org-admin history: time, user, number, location, recording, SIP invite.

items.title: WEM
items.snippet: Workforce, quality, analytics, surveys, and recording. Native suite and a Verint partnership are both on the product page.

items.title: GenAI Studio
items.snippet: Knowledge and prompts for Five9 AI apps. This lab does not name a default model.

items.title: Studio task key
items.snippet: The key copied from a ChatBot task into VCC for a digital IVA.

items.title: Agent Desktop Plus
items.snippet: The single agent screen. Same underlying technology as the prebuilt CRM adapters, per the desktop page.

items.title: Retention
items.snippet: Separate clocks for audio, E911 recordings, agent data, campaign state, domains, and DIDs.

items.title: RFC 3261
items.snippet: The SIP specification. It does not choose your dial plan.

items.title: RFC 4733
items.snippet: Telephone events, the usual way DTMF rides in the media.

items.title: The DNIS does not answer.
items.snippet: Is the inbound campaign running, or only built? Is this DNIS on that campaign? Did a schedule stop the campaign while leaving the number assigned?

items.title: Callers land on a queue nobody staffed.
items.snippet: Open the Skill Transfer module. See whether a skill is selected. Check the Default skill before you blame the carrier.

items.title: The agent hears silence, or the caller does.
items.snippet: Confirm signaling is up. A 200 OK does not prove RTP. If the firewall is not stateful, return UDP was not allowed. Compare softphone and WebRTC. WebRTC still needs the RTP range, plus STUN.

items.title: Voice is live and the CRM pane is blank.
items.snippet: The adapter uses HTTPS and Secure WebSocket. A proxy that strips WSS fails the pop and leaves the call. Name the adapter and the CRM release before you restart the phone.

items.title: The agent cannot paste a phone number.
items.snippet: Check whether the campaign is in TCPA manual touch. Manual touch expects a typed number and enables Dial on a match. Pasting is the control working, not a browser bug.

items.title: Customers hear a click and no agent.
items.snippet: Name the mode. Preview does not outdial. Predictive does. Read the abandon field. This lab will not invent the percent. Predictive guidance on the product page is about larger teams. Quote the page you mean.

items.title: A test 911 call would send responders to the old HQ.
items.snippet: The address has to be the room the person is in. A DID pointed at a corporate lobby is not a dispatchable location. MyE911 history is the place to see time, user, number, location, recording, and SIP invite.

items.title: Standard reports are missing for a supervisor.
items.snippet: The user needs the reporting role and a reporting permission. A wallboard feed is not the standard-report permission. Call variables stay invisible until the edit permission and the reporting flag.

items.title: The audio you need is gone.
items.snippet: Name which clock: audio, E911 recording, agent data, campaign state, the call log, or the DID. Screen recording bandwidth is not the same fact as retention. The retention page is the policy. A domain setting can be shorter.

items.title: The IVA will not return the caller to a person.
items.snippet: Confirm the Studio region matches the task you copied. The VCC side wants the task key, not a nickname. The handoff needs a named skill. Default is a queue, not a compliment.
